audit_items.proof_trace: Liquidation eligibility is determined using EMA prices (via `debts_value_usd_for_liquidation` / `collaterals_usd_for_liquidation` calling `get_price`), but the amount of collateral seized is calculated using raw Pyth spot prices (`get_spot_price`, L1045-46) with only a basic staleness check — no EMA/spot deviation guard. This breaks the property: all other sensitive paths use `get_price_with_check` (EMA + deviation check), but the seize calculation uses a more volatile and inconsistent price source. The 30-second Pyth staleness window (PRICE_FEED_DELAY_SECONDS) further allows a liquidator to choose which VAA to submit before calling liquidate, picking the moment when the spot price of collateral was lowest (or debt highest).
audit_items.attack_scenario: A liquidator monitors Pyth off-chain feeds for a moment when spot price of collateral temporarily drops relative to EMA (e.g., 8% dip during a sell-off, within the 10% ema_spot_tolerance). They submit that Pyth VAA (within the 30-second staleness window) to refresh the oracle's spot price, then immediately call liquidate. The position is eligible for liquidation per EMA-based check, but the seized collateral amount is computed using the depressed spot price — resulting in ~8% over-seizure of collateral relative to EMA-fair-value on the position, at the borrower's expense.
